inputs.original_text: That “8 million” figure is just the organizers’ claim, and authorities still haven’t provided a count. That silence is convenient: it leaves the headline free to turn scattered events into a supposedly unified national wave against Trump. The organizers’ claims of about one million more people and 600 more events than in October are part of the same sales pitch, not independent verification. This looks like coordinated narrative-building—using scale and repetition to manufacture momentum and make opposition seem more decisive than the evidence shows.
inputs.modified_text: The “8 million” figure is unverified, and authorities still haven’t provided a count. That silence looks less like a gap than a useful part of the operation: organizers can sell a story of rising momentum while officials leave the numbers unchallenged. The claims of about one million more people and 600 more events than in October may be less evidence than coordinated messaging designed to make opposition look inevitable. Either way, the public is being asked to accept a narrative without independent verification.
